definition: A substance that no chemical reaction can split into simpler substances; all its atoms have the same atomic number.
A substance of two or more elements held together by chemical bonds in a fixed ratio, with properties different from those elements.
Two or more elements or compounds together in any proportions, not bonded to each other, so physical methods can separate them.
The substance that dissolves in a solvent to make a solution.
The substance, usually a liquid, that a solute dissolves in to make a solution.
Purifying a solid by dissolving it in a little hot solvent, filtering, then cooling so pure crystals form while soluble impurities stay in solution.
Separating a liquid from a mixture by boiling it and condensing the vapour, using differences in boiling point.
The model that all matter is made of constantly moving particles, whose spacing, motion and attractions explain the states of matter and changes of state.
Labels after each formula in an equation giving its state: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas and (aq) dissolved in water.
A measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance; it is not the same as heat.
The SI unit of temperature, K, starting at absolute zero; a step of 1 K equals a step of 1 °C, and $T$ in K $= t$ in °C $+ 273.15$.
